title: Uploading and Downloading Files
learning_outcomes: Explain how uploading and downloading files affects an API contract or implementation.
Apply the key ideas from multipart form data to a concrete API example.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on uploading and downloading files in asynchronous apis, webhooks, and external integrations. You will connect multipart form data to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: Uploading and Downloading Files matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying multipart form data deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: External work needs bounded timeouts, verified webhooks, duplicate-event handling, observable job status, and recovery logic. troubleshooting: Check the exact HTTP method, path, status, header, media type, and payload before changing implementation code.

Testing only the happy path and ignoring malformed, unauthorized, conflicting, duplicate, or dependency-failure cases.
Publishing an example without checking version assumptions, sensitive-data exposure, and the expected output.
